clue.text: Crafty operator's cheesy product not available inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the abbreviation for not available sits within the dairy word

parts.note: curd is the product from which cheese is made
N/A, written NA, is the standard short form for not available

explanation.surface: A sly dealer peddles cheese that cannot be bought.
explanation.walkthrough: Cunard is the shipping line; in this puzzle every clue with two lengths loses UN in the grid, so the entry is CARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Cunard runs ocean liners, so it is literally an operator of craft, a ship company.

clue.text: Buttoned up Swedish pop group member?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a knitted jacket that fastens with buttons, read cryptically as the thing buttoned up
second meaning: one of The ..., the Swedish band, with the question mark flagging the whimsy

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped member of a Scandinavian band.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cardigans were a Swedish pop group of the 1990s ('Lovefool'); the question mark admits a member is only a cardigan by a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted jacket that buttons down the front, and the band's name makes a member one.

clue.text: International combination used by Pablo Casals

indicators.note: the letters are used by the cellist's name, sitting across its two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first name and the start of the surname

explanation.surface: The famous Catalan cellist employs some worldwide alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a grouping of nations allied for a common purpose, such as the Eastern bloc.

clue.text: Are there more surprises in store from West Derby, say, retail chain?

definitions.text: Are there more surprises in store

parts.note: a derby is a bowler hat, given as an example of a hat
Next is a British high-street clothing chain

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Liverpool district's shops hold more surprises.
explanation.walkthrough: West Derby is a district of Liverpool, but here Derby is the hat; Next is a British fashion retailer.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'what next?' asks, in exasperation, what fresh surprise is coming.

clue.text: But not if unlikely weather for lying on beach topless

indicators.note: topless says the word loses its first letter, and fits the beach picture

parts.words: unlikely weather for lying on beach
parts.note: sunless weather is not what sunbathers want

explanation.surface: Sunbathing topless would not suit a dull day.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction means except if, the same sense as but not if in a condition.

clue.text: Money given to contemptible sort for a bit of a roll

parts.note: bread is slang for money
a crumb is slang for a worthless person

explanation.surface: Cash handed to a lowlife in return for a scrap of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadcrumb is a tiny fragment of bread, so it is a small piece of a bread roll.

clue.text: Hearing test with a hair style thrown in

indicators.note: thrown in means the hairdo is put into the word for a test

parts.note: a trial is a test, and the clue's 'with a' reminds us the word contains the letter A
a bun is hair coiled at the back of the head

explanation.surface: An audiometry check with a new hairdo included.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid entry drops UN, as in all two-length clues here, leaving TRIBAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body that holds hearings, and the word can mean the hearing itself.

clue.text: Folly — woman has one put up inside

indicators.note: inside places the upturned article within the woman's name

parts.note: Lucy is a woman's name

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word for one is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: an means one, as in an apple

explanation.surface: Madness: a woman keeps someone lodged at her place.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid entry drops UN, leaving LACY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunacy is extreme foolishness, the same idea as folly.

clue.text: Flipping Virginia's to get sick benefit!

indicators.note: flipping means the state abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia; the 's stands for has
to ail is to fall ill

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that Virginia must fall ill to claim sickness pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or advantage, so it means to benefit.

clue.text: Black man not spaced out by song gets voluntary payments

parts.note: Blackman written as one word is the actress Honor Blackman, so the clue wants her first name
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned man, bewildered by music, collects donations.
explanation.walkthrough: Honor Blackman played Pussy Galore in Goldfinger; closing up 'Black man' gives her surname, which points to her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Honoraria are fees paid as a courtesy for services where no fixed charge is owed.

clue.text: Object of tributary work: drowning headless Star Wars knight, Ginger, in river

indicators.note: the river closes over the other pieces as if they drown in it

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: headless means the knight loses his first letter

parts.note: the Jedi are the knights of Star Wars
Ginger is a common name for a ginger cat

explanation.surface: A fan tribute in which a beheaded Jedi and a redhead end up in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Tributary here means paying tribute, not a stream feeding a river, though the river in the clue plays on that.
explanation.definitionFit: A dedicatee is the person a book or piece of music is dedicated to, the recipient of the tribute.

clue.text: One old g-governor's place for those in order

parts.note: a bey was an Ottoman provincial governor, and the stammered g- tells us to double its first letter

explanation.surface: A stammering former governor's home for people kept in line.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey houses monks or nuns, members of a religious order.

clue.text: Source of cover for the modest new gift almost costing nothing

definitions.text: Source of cover for the modest

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of gift are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

indicators.note: almost says the word for costing nothing is not used whole, losing one letter

parts.note: free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A modest new present that is nearly free.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually, almost drops the first letter of the word for costing nothing rather than its last.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve covered themselves with fig leaves, so the fig tree supplies modesty's covering.

clue.text: Not averse to air of success

parts.note: being for something means being in favour of it
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Happy to hear a triumphant melody.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid entry drops UN, leaving FORTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune can mean prosperity or good luck, the sense of making one's fortune.

clue.text: Where to fix your car and make it posh again?

definitions.text: Where to fix your car and make it posh again?

parts.note: the plain reading: a garage that repairs vehicles
swap the two pairs of letters in posh and the word becomes shop

explanation.walkthrough: Repair is read as re-pair: PO-SH re-paired gives SH-OP, so the second half of the clue makes posh into the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A repair shop is a garage or workshop where broken machines, cars included, are mended.

clue.text: Pap-fed but not fed pap

parts.note: pap is an old word for a nipple, so fed at the breast
pap is also soft mushy baby food, which a breastfed baby is not given

explanation.walkthrough: Pap has two meanings, nipple and baby mush; the clue plays the first against the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A suckled infant is one nursed at the breast rather than given food from a spoon.

clue.text: Steadfast when relative enters Dracula-like and one's ousted

indicators.note: enters means the family member goes inside the vampire word
ousted means the article is thrown out of the vampire word

parts.note: Dracula is one of the undead
a is one; the 's is a contracted is
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Holding firm when a kinsman turns vampire and a family member is expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Two UNs drop from the grid entry here, leaving DATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Undaunted means not discouraged or intimidated, which is resolute and unwavering.

clue.text: Approached and hastily assembled

definitions.meaning: first meaning: came running up to someone
second meaning: to run up a garment or shed is to make it quickly

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses use different meanings of run: moving quickly and sewing or building in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both dashing towards someone and knocking something together quickly.

clue.text: Top of old letter's given new heading

indicators.note: given new heading means the word's first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: runic means belonging to runes, the old Germanic letters

explanation.surface: An ancient inscription's title is changed.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid entry drops UN, leaving TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose garment for the upper body, a top in clothing terms.

clue.text: Sheltered exotic ocean dip

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange or outlandish, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A swim in faraway waters somewhere protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Canopied means covered by an overhead awning, so shaded and protected from the weather.

clue.text: After hike, group given a tip

indicators.note: the group's word comes after the word for hike

parts.note: to hike prices is to put them up
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Walkers given a gratuity at the end of a trek.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset something is to overturn it, which is what tipping it over does.

clue.text: The military oldies flummoxed by your text-messaged reversal

indicators.note: flummoxed means baffled, so the letters of oldies are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

indicators.note: reversal says the texting form of your is turned round

parts.note: yr is the shortened form of your used in texts

explanation.surface: Old people baffled when a phone message gives them a U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiery is soldiers collectively, so it can stand for an army or the armed forces.

clue.text: A course getting stuffed when top removed

definitions.note: an easting is a course or distance sailed due east

indicators.note: top removed in an across clue means the first letter goes

parts.note: feasting is eating one's fill

explanation.surface: One part of a meal being gobbled after the lid comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A course' wants to be part of a meal, which fits the stuffing; it is a direction of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: In navigation an easting is a heading or distance run towards the east.

clue.text: Ray's newspaper fair

definitions.note: read as 'ray is': the rays of the sun

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
fair hair is light hair

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray's newspaper is even-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid entry drops UN, leaving SLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunlight is the light that arrives from the sun in its beams of radiance.

clue.text: Creative stylizing: no sin but gaudy and tacky

indicators.note: creative suggests inventing, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
no sin tells us the three letters of sin are taken out of stylizing before the rest is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Inventive design that is harmless yet loud and cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of sin are scattered through stylizing, so each is removed separately before the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitzy describes showy, flashy glamour, ostentatious in a vulgar way.

clue.text: Swanky type was bloody got at

parts.note: a nob is an upper-class person
bled means lost blood

explanation.surface: A posh person who was bleeding had been attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: To nobble is to tamper with or bribe, the sense in which a juror or a horse is got at.

clue.text: Joy, supreme composer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: Sir Arthur ..., Master of the Queen's Music, the top post for a British composer

explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Bliss held the post of Master of the Queen's Music, which makes him supreme among royal composers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bliss is perfect happiness, and it is also the surname of the English composer Arthur Bliss.

clue.text: Petty Officers raised terse term of abuse, acquiring shiner

indicators.note: acquiring means the upturned insult takes the shiner inside it
raised in a down clue means the insult is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: SOB is the terse form of son of a bitch
the sun is what shines

explanation.surface: Naval non-commissioned officers snarl a curt insult and get a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shiner' wants to be a black eye, following the brawl; it is the sun. The grid entry drops UN, leaving BOSS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosun, the boatswain, is the petty officer in charge of a ship's rigging and deck crew.

clue.text: One's inept, dropping round and fiddling with radio, being a solicitor

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am, one being the speaker

indicators.note: dropping means one of the round letters is let fall from the word for inept

parts.note: poor means of low skill
O is round in shape
tuning is adjusting a radio to a station

explanation.surface: A useless person twiddling a wireless dial trying to work as a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' wants to be a lawyer; it is someone who solicits. The grid entry drops UN, leaving IMPORTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Importuning is pestering persistently with requests, which is what soliciting someone means.

clue.text: Go with the flow, sustained by hefty faggots with lashings of natural fibre?

definitions.text: Go with the flow, sustained by hefty faggots with lashings of natural fibre?

parts.note: to travel downstream on a floating platform, drifting with the current

parts.words: sustained by hefty faggots with lashings of natural fibre
parts.note: the vessel is bundles of logs or sticks (faggots) tied together with rope

explanation.walkthrough: Faggots here are bundles of sticks, and lashings are the ropes tying them, not generous helpings of a meatball supper.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat floating platform of lashed timber, and to raft is to travel on one downriver.

clue.text: Sell up and get a round in

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for sell is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to flog is slang for to sell

explanation.surface: Cash in and buy everyone drinks at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a round in' wants to be buying drinks, the British pub custom; it means playing a round on a course.
explanation.definitionFit: A round is one complete circuit of a course, eighteen holes, so to play one is golf.

clue.text: Get drunk without companion, name of 'Snitch'

definitions.note: snitch is old slang for the nose; a noun, like the answer

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the drink word goes round the others

parts.note: to sozzle is to make or get drunk
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: An informer called Snitch drinks heavily, alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snitch' wants to be an informer; it is old slang for the nose, as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnozzle is jocular slang for a nose, especially a big one.

clue.text: Formal grounding of some perisher

parts.note: read as a ceremonious putting into the ground, not a basic education
someone who has perished, that is died

explanation.walkthrough: Grounding usually means basic training; here it is a burial. The grid entry drops UN, leaving FERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral is the ceremony with which a dead person is buried or cremated.
